translation_notes: the mechanical draft wrote `self.initial_graph += g{ }` at every one of the six add sites; per the batch's confirmed bias, corrected to one `@graph self.initial_graph` (declared once, function-level, never reassigned) followed by six `+{ }`/`-{ }` writing straight into the live graph.

two real `;`-fusions, no more: `shacl:path` and (in the fallback block) `a shacl:PropertyShape ; shacl:path` are each two back-to-back .add() with nothing between them. Every OTHER add in this function is separated from its neighbour by an `if pom["datatype"]/["termType"]/["template_length"] is not None:` guard or a `for` loop -- fusing across those would require moving the guard/loop, which the no-refactoring rule forbids. Same shape as the two add_run_shared_subject regions already done in this batch (the redefine-style region and MRHGraph.add_relevance): most of a shared-subject run's adds are NOT fusable once real control flow sits between them, and this region is the extreme case of that (six candidate adds, only two pairs actually adjacent).

each remove/add here is an 'erase then repose' pair on ONE predicate at a time (self.initial_graph.remove((s, p, None)) then .add((s, p, new))), same pattern as the redefine precedent in the remove stratum -- but the datatype guard removes on TWO predicates (nodeKind AND datatype) before adding one. Piege 'a -{ } multi-motifs JOINT': -{ shacl:nodeKind ?o ; shacl:datatype ?o } would be a DELETE WHERE needing BOTH to exist before deleting either, which is not what two independent .remove() calls mean. Kept as two separate -{ }, never merged, exactly as the remove stratum's own guidance says.

self.initial_graph.value(shape_identifier, self.shaclNS.minLength) -> m{ {shape_identifier} shacl:minLength ?o }.first(): the mechanical draft left this g.value() call untouched even though it sits inside this very region (trav_single_value's idiom, INSTRUCTIONS.md SS2). Translated it too, since 'always the most specific construction' is not limited to the region's primary stratum. Not fused into the surrounding m{ }/+{ } (there are none it could join without changing cardinality) and the subsequent remove uses the interpolated {value} it read, not a wildcard -- .remove((s, p, value)) targets one specific term, not every match, so -{ } does too.

self.shaclNS.X (predicate/class names, e.g. .path, .datatype, .PropertyShape) -> shacl:X: constant attribute access on a Namespace instance ALWAYS bound to the same fixed IRI (http://www.w3.org/ns/shacl#) in the real ShapeAdjustment.__init__ (verified against the pinned commit) and in ShapeAdjustmentStub here -- same ns_def_local idiom as `NS = Namespace(...) in a function -> @prefix`, just instance-attribute-scoped rather than function-local. RDF.type -> `a`. rdf:/rdfs:/xsd:/owl: (the draft's four prefixes) were never written as a single literal prefixed name anywhere in this function's actual body and were dropped; shacl: is the only one this region uses.

self.updateShape/self.getConstraints/self.updateCombinationShape/self.validatePath are NOT part of the extracted region (sibling methods on the same class) and stay opaque Python calls -- no island syntax to write for them. context_shim.py copies all four VERBATIM from the pinned commit (none do I/O) so the fixtures below exercise the real logic.

missing bindings: adjust_pom is a bare method (self.initial_graph, self.shape_path, self.findNS, self.findPS, self.adjusted_shape, self.iterator, self.shaclNS, self.random_number, plus the four sibling methods above) -- none in the extracted context. Restored via context_shim.ShapeAdjustmentStub, duck-typing only what this region touches, not the rest of the real ShapeAdjustment (RML parsing, adjust_sm's shared_sm_identifier bookkeeping). self.random_number (upstream: 3000 random.randint(1000,9999) values, only ever .pop()'d) is a fixed deterministic list here -- this region never inspects its values, only consumes them, so determinism matters and the RNG's actual distribution does not.

a demo(initial_graph, shape_path, findNS, pom_list, iterator) harness (identical on both sides) wraps the call, since adjust_pom mutates `self` rather than returning anything and ShapeAdjustmentStub has no __eq__ (comparing self directly would always fail) -- same pattern as the JonAnderAsua and MRHGraph regions in this stratum. Returns the graph plus adjusted_shape/findPS as strings.

driver.py: four fixtures, each its own zero-arg callable (not a plain (args, kwargs) tuple) so run_pair's one-call-per-side gives each side a FRESH Graph() -- demo mutates its graph in place, and a shared Graph object would let the original run's writes leak into the translated run's starting state, a silent false-green. Together the four cover: (1) a fresh shape_identifier with datatype+termType+template_length all firing against a pre-seeded graph, (2) the same shape_identifier matched twice so the second pass takes the self.adjusted_shape re-adjustment branch (self.updateShape), (3) the multi-path branch reaching self.getConstraints/self.updateCombinationShape, (4) no shape_path match at all, reaching the fallback block including its for/else -- which has no `break`, so the else is UNCONDITIONAL in real Python and was translated that way, not 'fixed'.
